fields.v: Project/tasks: 200 FeatureBench tasks (Lite 30) from 24 Python repositories, in Docker environments. Configurations: 7 scaffold+model pairs (OpenHands with 4 models, Gemini-CLI, Claude Code, Codex); reasoning levels differ by model. Baseline: OpenHands framework called 'baseline'; no condition without the interface specification except in the ablation. Held constant: tasks, problem statements, environments, F2P/P2P tests, internet access without browser tools, anti-cheating (blacklisted URLs, log inspection); OpenHands step limit 500 (limits for other scaffolds not stated). Acceptance tests: repository F2P and P2P unit tests run with pytest. Repetitions: none stated. Human intervention: none during runs

fields.v: Full set: best % Resolved Codex + GPT-5.1-Codex 12.5%, Claude Code + Opus 4.5 11.0%, OpenHands + Opus 4.5 10.5%; others 3.5-5.5%. Best % Passed OpenHands + Opus 4.5 45.53%. All configurations use >1M input tokens per task (2.0M-8.1M). Claude Opus 4.5 resolves 74.4% on SWE-bench Verified but 5.2% on the SWE-bench-shared FeatureBench subset. L2 (from scratch) lower than L1 for the stronger configurations (e.g. 13.9 vs 5.9 for Codex). Removing interfaces lowers resolved/passed; visible tests raise resolved by 43-50 points; steps 50 -> 100 helps, 100 -> 500 marginal. Rankings consistent between Lite and Full. No significance tests

fields.v: Distinguished configurations within a narrow range (3.5-12.5% resolved on 200 tasks); % Passed gives finer resolution. Repeatability: single runs, no variance reported; manual verification ablation shows small differences (GPT-5.1-Codex 16.7 vs 20.0). Limitations stated by the authors: risk of data leakage growing as agents participate in feature development; Gemini 3 Pro failures due to tool-schema mismatch. No other limitations of the comparison method stated

fields.v: Reporting inconsistencies: abstract highlights Claude Opus 4.5 at 11.0% as state of the art, while Codex + GPT-5.1-Codex is best at 12.5% (p. 1 vs Table 2, p. 6); Table 5 'Original' GPT-5.1-Codex on Lite is 16.7 resolved / 53.9 passed (p. 8) while Table 2 Lite gives 20.0 / 60.22 (which matches the 'Verified' row); likewise for Gemini-3-Pro the Table 5 'Verified' % Passed 43.4 matches Gemini-CLI Lite 43.38 in Table 2, while 'Original' 42.4 matches neither Gemini row (45.14, 43.38), so the Table 2 Lite results appear to use the manually verified prompts (scaffold of Table 5 not stated); the text says L2 (from scratch) has 'lower resolved rates' (p. 10), but in Table 8 L2 resolved is equal or higher than L1 for 3 of 7 configurations (DeepSeek-V3.2 4.8 vs 5.9, OpenHands + Gemini 4.2 vs 5.9, Gemini-CLI 4.8 vs 5.9) and L2 % Passed is higher for 4 (e.g. Qwen3-Coder 22.4 vs 35.2); Appendix D says experiments use 'a unified OpenHands scaffold with multiple LLM backends (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Qwen)' (p. 18), but GPT was run only with Codex and four scaffolds were used; Section 4.1.1 heading calls OpenHands the 'baseline'. Claude Code '(routing)' not explained. Table 4 SWE-bench Verified column partly garbled in text extraction (mini-SWE-agent 60.00, 55.40, 74.20, 74.40; one OpenHands value 69.60). L1/L2 task counts not stated (166/34, rebuilt from Table 8 percentages and the Full resolved counts, e.g. Codex 23 + 2 = 25 = 12.5% of 200). Code: github.com/LiberCoders/FeatureBench; dataset released. No pre-registration. Programming language: Python
